text:
ConocoPhillips rose 2.7% today to $154.03, reversing losses from earlier in the week. The gain comes as oil prices have stabilized after a brief dip on Monday's diplomatic news—U.S. crude is trading at $103.37 per barrel, and the stock has climbed 5% over the past two weeks as geopolitical tensions around Iran keep energy prices elevated and volatile. The recent reports of U.S.-Iran peace talks lowered prices momentarily, but both sides are reportedly preparing for additional military strikes, which has kept the upside pressure on crude alive.

The wider backdrop helps: oil majors have reported strong refining earnings as fuel supplies have tightened, so even with Trump's pledges to lower energy costs, the structural conditions supporting higher oil prices remain in place. A large gap between U.S. crude ($103) and world oil ($123) also suggests continued supply concerns that favor producers.
